task_title: CLI: Make bail on error the default in more situations
problem_statement: The DuckDB CLI shell does not stop processing SQL when it encounters an error while reading from non-interactive (piped) stdin. When multiple SQL statements are piped to the shell and one of them fails, the shell continues executing the remaining statements instead of halting. Users expect that a SQL error in a pipeline or script causes the CLI to exit immediately with a non-zero status, matching the behaviour of `.bail on`. The shell should default to bail-on-error mode whenever stdin is not a terminal (i.e. isatty(0) returns 0).
problem_statement_variant: The DuckDB CLI shell continues executing SQL statements after an error when reading from a non-interactive stdin (e.g., a pipe or file redirect). Fix the shell so that it defaults to bail-on-error mode whenever stdin is not a terminal.
hints: Look at how the shell initializes bail_on_error and where it checks whether stdin is interactive using isatty().
